I vaguely remember Glenn McCarthy had several clubs in town and that was one of them, I thought the Cork Club but that has been identified as atop the Central National Bank Bldg. I know it was a gay club in the early 70s, the Palace or Plantation or something like that, Scott...

haif_threads.title: Hanover Montrose: Multifamily At 3400 Montrose Blvd.
haif_threads.excerpt: A new 26 story high-rise is going to be built on Montrose where the current M2M clothing store/SkyBar building stands...According to my realtor, the property has been purchased, along with a home and several townhomes behind the building. They will all be torn down....the new building will have 2 floors of retail, 5 floors of parking,...

0052240000015.source_citation: Dating to c. 1850–1870 on Lubbock Street, one of the earliest surviving mid-19th-century vernacular cottages in the Old Sixth Ward (Protected Landmark).

0052100000001.source_citation: Just around the corner at 1920 Kane Street, an 1875 Victorian cottage designated as a City of Houston Protected Landmark.

0201540000011.source_citation: Two blocks north and one block east on Cortlandt Street—an ornate 1902 Queen Anne cottage with Eastlake spindlework by architect R. D. Steele.

0201530000017.source_citation: Back on the 1400 block of Heights Boulevard, a stately 1920 Prairie Style residence overlooking the landscaped esplanade trail.

0050210000005.source_citation: Directly across Andrews Street—built in 1927 for Fourth Ward minister, brickyard owner, and civic leader Rev. Ned P. Pullum (Protected Landmark).

0010570000009.source_citation: Three blocks west at Main and Texas—erected by William Marsh Rice's estate in 1913 on the exact corner where the 1837 Capitol of the Republic of Texas stood.

0102490000010.source_citation: Midway down the esplanade—a 1912 Prairie Style mansion designed by Olle Lorehn and Birdsall P. Briscoe.

0102490000012.source_citation: Two doors west at 22 Courtlandt Place, a 1917 Georgian Revival residence designed by renowned Houston architect Birdsall P. Briscoe.

0102490000013.source_citation: Next door at 24 Courtlandt Place, a 1919 Tudor Revival mansion designed by Gulf Building architect Alfred C. Finn.

0041400000004.source_citation: One block north in the Avondale East Historic District, a 1917 Prairie Style residence by the Russell Brown Company (Protected Landmark).
